summary.text: The speed of light is the speed of electromagnetic waves; in a vacuum it is a universal constant called c, exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.
In a vacuum it is the same for every observer however they move, and it is the upper limit for how fast information, matter or energy can travel.
Light is slower inside materials such as glass or water, and the ratio of c to its speed in a material is called the refractive index.

facts.value: The metre is defined from the speed of light

items.prompt: A spacecraft races toward a flashlight beam while a friend stands still. What speed does each measure for the beam in a vacuum?

options.label: The spacecraft measures a higher speed than the friend
The friend measures a higher speed than the spacecraft
The same speed, c, for both
Each gets a speed set by how fast the lamp moves

items.explain: The speed of light in vacuum is the same for all observers, regardless of their relative velocity or the source's motion.

items.prompt: You look at a distant star tonight. In what sense are you looking at the past?

options.label: Light takes a long time to cross the distance
Stars dim quickly after they are seen
Telescopes always delay what they show
The star's own clock runs slow

items.explain: Light travels at a finite speed, so much starlight seen on Earth left its source long ago.

items.prompt: An engineer asks whether a spaceship with mass could be pushed until it moves at exactly the speed of light. What is the answer?

options.label: Yes, once it has enough fuel
Yes, but only in a vacuum
Yes, if observers move along with it
No, it can approach that speed but never reach it

items.explain: Particles with nonzero rest mass can be accelerated toward c but can never reach it, in any frame of reference.

items.prompt: Light slows down inside glass. What is the ratio of its vacuum speed to its speed in the glass called?

options.label: The Doppler shift
The refractive index
The wavelength
The rest mass

items.explain: The ratio between c and the speed v in a material is the refractive index n = c/v.

items.prompt: The speed of light is quoted as a precise figure with no uncertainty at all. Why can that be?

options.label: Instruments now measure it to endless digits
Light never changes speed in any situation
Scientists voted to round it to that number
The metre is defined from how far light travels

items.explain: By international agreement a metre is defined as the path light covers in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second, which fixes the value exactly.

items.prompt: Rømer watched Jupiter's moon Io carefully. What did its apparent motion help him show about light?

options.label: Light does not arrive instantly
Light travels faster than any wave
Light bends when passing a planet
Light speed depends on the planet's mass

items.explain: Rømer first demonstrated that light does not travel instantaneously by studying the apparent motion of Io.
